The diversion, prompted by Houthi attacks on shipping, has pushed transfer capacity in the Gulf of Oman to its ceiling, according to Reuters, which cited unnamed trading sources and analysts. The freight spike is the clearest sign yet that the physical crude market is paying a growing premium simply to move barrels safely.
Buyers are absorbing the cost of longer routes and scarce tanker slots without bidding the headline number sharply higher, at least for now.
Saudi barrels take the long way around
Yanbu sits on the Red Sea, and Red Sea traffic has become a liability. With Houthi strikes making the route dangerous, Saudi flows have shifted, and the crude that would normally load cleanly is instead being handled through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman.

* Pensana VAC rare earth offtake agreement anchors Western mine-to-magnet strategy
* VAC
Pensana VAC rare earth offtake agreement marks a pivotal step in building a Western rare earths supply chain. Pensana will supply mixed rare earth carbonate from its Longonjo project in Angola to Vacuumschmelze (VAC) under a five-year contract.
This Pensana VAC rare earth offtake agreement underpins new US magnet capacity and links African upstream resources with Western downstream processing.
Pensana VAC rare earth offtake agreement will initially channel Longonjo’s MREC into VAC’s growing magnet footprint. Pensana plans to start production at Longonjo in late 2026, targeting 20,000 t/yr of mixed rare earth carbonate. The company ultimately aims to double output to 40,000 t/yr in a second phase.
Meanwhile, VAC is scaling its eVAC permanent magnet plant in Sumter, South Carolina. The Pensana VAC rare earth offtake agreement is designed to support 2,000 t/yr of NdFeB magnet output, rising to 12,000 t/yr by 2029.
By locking in MREC feedstock, eVAC can plan long-term capacity and qualify Western supply for automotive, wind and defense customers.
VAC is also racing to develop heavy rare earth-free magnet alloys to reduce dependence on China.
Its latest NdFeB alloy eliminates terbium and dysprosium, which are currently produced at scale almost exclusively in China. As a result, the Pensana VAC rare earth offtake agreement complements alloy innovation by anchoring a diversified feedstock base.

The demonstration is significant because GPS denial is increasingly becoming a constant presence on the battlefield, which represents a problem for military aircraft and uncrewed systems.
“Leveraging our proven MagNav technologies and drone platform expertise, the flight test with Northrop Grumman further demonstrates the ease by which our AQNav software can be integrated into unmanned systems at the speed and scale required by leading defense organizations.” – Luca Ferrara, General Manager of Navigation at SandboxAQ
“The platform’s navigation system can then weigh AQNav’s positioning against its other onboard sources.”

Refinancing risk in private credit appears increasingly differentiated. While the aggregate contractual maturity schedule is extended and most analysed positions continue to be reported at fair value close to cost, valuation pressure is concentrated within a smaller subset of borrowers approaching maturity.

As a result, the future trajectory of private credit may depend less on the volume of debt maturing and more on how lenders, sponsors and borrowers respond as those maturities approach.
For investors, the key challenge is therefore not identifying whether a maturity wall exists. It is determining which borrowers can successfully navigate it.

The military is working to make its bases energy self-sufficient through the deployment of "microgrids." What it learns will be useful to civilians as well.
One way the military is meeting that challenge is developing microgrids , which are way cooler than they sound.
The two types of DOD bases face the same challenge, but for different reasons. In Afghanistan, the diesel generators that provide electricity at bases are the top consumer of fuel on the battlefield.
One way to reduce that fuel use is to generate more power on site, through distributed generation technologies like solar or waste-to-power plants. Another is to use that power more efficiently. And another is to network the base’s power sources and loads together into a microgrid that can be managed intelligently.
Anyway, that’s the battlefield microgrid stuff, and it’s really cool. But I want to focus on the state-side “stationary” bases. As it happens, they are also plugged into a primitive grid — namely, the aging, shaky U.S. power grid. The military doesn’t trust it. It’s one thing if you’re at home and the lights flicker.
If successful, even a total blackout of the larger grid would not affect power on the base. And though the primary purpose is security-related, it would also help DOD meet its clean-energy goals.

candidates.source_name: Operators Leverage Technology, Infrastructure To Grow Permian
candidates.snippet:
Across the basin, service providers such as Goodnight Midstream continue to add infrastructure to accommodate expanding throughput demand while upstream players such as Devon Energy, Ovintiv, Ring Energy, EON Resources and Diversified Energy take advantage of advanced systems and growing downhole expertise.
Through an agreement to acquire Birch Permian Holdings, Diversified Energy plans to gain a sizable inventory of producing assets in the Midland Basin near some of its other assets. About 75% of the Birch wells were completed in 2022 or earlier, meaning Diversified has numerous opportunities to enhance production through recompletions and workovers.
With upstream players continuing to go full speed ahead in the Delaware Basin, Goodnight Midstream is adding water pipeline capacity to expand service to operators.

candidates.title: Dallas Fed’s Third Quarter Survey Highlights Continued Growth
candidates.source_name: Dallas Fed’s Third Quarter Survey Highlights Continued Growth
candidates.snippet:
The survey draws on responses from 83 exploration and production firms and 42 oil field service firms located in the Eleventh District, which includes Texas, southern New Mexico and northern Louisiana. Data collection took place between Sept. 16-24.
“Among oil field services firms, the input cost index stayed elevated but edged down from 64.4 to 60.4. Among E&P firms, the finding and development costs index and the lease operating expenses index were relatively unchanged at 41.5 and 43.9, respectively,” the Fed details.
“All cost indexes were above their series averages, suggesting costs are growing at a faster-than-average pace.”
Even so, oil field service firms reported improvement in most indicators. “The equipment utilization index increased from 31.9 in the second quarter to 41.9 in the third,” the Fed relates.
“The operating margin index remained positive but decreased from 52.2 to 37.2, suggesting margins expanded at a slightly slower pace. The prices received for services index also remained positive but declined slightly from 24.5 to 16.3.”

China Oilfield Services expanding fleet with 59 offshore vessels
China Oilfield Services Limited (COSL) has issued a procurement notice to build 59 offshore work vessels across six designs, kicking off one of China’s most substantial offshore support fleet renewal programmes in recent years.
The newbuild portfolio covers Anchor Handling Tug Supply (AHTS) vessels, Platform Supply Vessels (PSVs), and oilfield standby‑and‑supply units for diverse offshore operational scenarios.
The breakdown includes four 15,000‑hp AHTS, six 12,000‑hp AHTS, three 8,000‑hp AHTS, fourteen 2,000‑dwt PSVs, twenty‑three 3,000‑dwt PSVs, seven 4,000‑dwt PSVs, one 6,500‑hp LNG‑fuelled standby‑and‑supply vessel (3,000 dwt with oil transfer capacity), and one 10,000‑hp LNG‑fuelled standby‑and‑supply vessel (4,000 dwt with oil transfer capacity).
Delivery will be phased from 2028 through to 2030.
Upon completion, the new fleet will strengthen comprehensive logistical support for China’s offshore oil‑and‑gas operations and accelerate green, intelligent upgrading of the country’s offshore work‑vessel fleet.
Related: Seadrill loses $55m appeal over Hercules rig redelivery
In parallel to the 59‑vessel initiative, the board has also cleared feasibility work for four high‑performance jack‑up drilling platforms. These new rigs will feature upgraded well‑control systems, automated drilling modules and specialised hardware optimised for long‑horizontal‑section shale‑oil development.

Ocean Oilfield enriches drilling fleet with jack-up rig acquisition
Ocean Oilfield, a UAE-headquartered service provider to offshore and onshore oil and gas companies, has completed the acquisition and ownership takeover of Ocean MVM (formerly Noble Resolve ), a GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC jack-up drilling rig.
The newly acquired jack-up drilling unit arrived in Malta on October 13 and is now being actively marketed and made available for immediate deployment, subject to contractual arrangements and operational requirements.
The unit officially joined the Ocean Oilfield fleet following the company’s acquisition announcement on December 9, 2025.
The takeover of jack-up drilling rig builds on Ocean Oilfield’s 40th anniversary celebrations in 2026, reflecting four decades of service, since its establishment in 1985, to the energy industry.
Sameer M, CEO of Ocean Oilfield, commented that the acquisition strengthens the company’s fleet and represents a significant step forward in its continued growth. He added that it reinforces operational capabilities and enhances the company’s ability to support clients across key global markets.
The new owner described the rig as an attractive option for operators for upcoming offshore campaigns worldwide.
Ocean Oilfield also noted that the GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC design series is known for its performance in challenging offshore and severe weather conditions.
